title: Shuram excursion (Ediacaran carbon isotope excursion)
summary: The Shuram excursion is the most negative carbon-isotope swing in Earth history, recorded in Ediacaran carbonate rocks in Oman, South Australia, south China and the southwestern United States. In the Wonoka Formation of South Australia it spans about 17 permil. It is placed after the roughly 580 Ma Gaskiers glaciation and before about 551 Ma, and whether it records the ocean or later rock alteration is still debated.

uncertainty.note: Husson et al. (2015): hosted in sediments younger than the 580 Ma Gaskiers glaciation and older than a 551 Ma ash bed in south China (551.1 ± 0.7 Ma, recovery only). Duration estimates range from 5 to 50 Myr and Le Guerroué (2010) says none of these excursions is firmly time constrained, so start and end are the bracketing ages, not an onset and end. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset. The id says 574 Ma; no opened page gives that figure.
